descriptionChirho: Masculine noun denoting a boil, skin ulcer, or inflamed sore, appearing primarily in the plague narratives (Exodus 9:9-11), Levitical skin disease laws (Leviticus 13:18-23), and the affliction of Hezekiah (2 Kings 20:7) and Job (Job 2:7). All four clusters represent the same medical/dermatological term with grammatical variation: with article (the boil), bare noun (boils), with preposition ב and suffix (with boils of), and with preposition ל (into boils). Multilingual glosses converge: Arabic دُمَّل/قُرُوح (boil/sores), Spanish úlcera/divieso (ulcer/boil), Korean 종기 (boil/abscess), Hindi फोड़े (boil), Swahili jipu/majipu (boil/boils). Single sense with no polysemy detected.
